newsitem.title: USA: Most US debt futures end lower, long end sags late.
newsitem.headline: Most US debt futures end lower, long end sags late.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished mostly lower in quiet post-holiday trading, still spooked by Thursday's technical breakdown and wary ahead of upcoming key data.
The long end sagged late and U.S. June Treasury bond futures ended just above their session low.

"The market's in bad shape," one T-bond futures trader said. "In fact, it was a pretty bad close considering where we were all day," he said. He estimated the high volume area for the day's session at 107-10/32 to 107-16/32.
Traders noted jitters ahead of key data later this week.

The National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) March index, February leading indicators and February construction spending are due Tuesday. On Friday, March non-farm payrolls data are to be released.

Many traders said the market would remain choppy heading into Friday with players bracing for signs of strength in the economy. They said they will watch closely for what those data portend for the Federal Reserve's May policy meeting.
March NAPM was forecast at 53.6 versus a 53.1 reading in February. Jobs were forecast to rise 182,000 in March compared with a 339,000 gain in February.
Oversold ideas after Thursday's breakdown on technicals and rate-hike fears supported June T-bonds earlier in the session, traders said.

"There may have been some bargain hunting going on all day with the market oversold, but those buyers couldn't get enough of a bounce to stay long overnight," said Don Pullen, E.D. and F. Man's bond trading floor manager.
He said the day's longs who liquidated near the end of trading helped push the thin market lower.
An early slate of economic data had little lasting effect on debt futures.

February's U.S. personal income rose 0.9 percent, its biggest one-month increase since June 1996. Spending gained 0.3 percent. Those compared to forecasts for respective gains of 0.8 percent and 0.4 percent.
Chicago Purchasing Managers March index was a shade firmer than forecast, at 57.5 versus 56.2 in February.
Traders pegged support for June at 106-22/32, the lowest price since last September.

June T-bonds closed down 5/32 at 107-7/32, T-notes lost 2/32 to 105-16/32, munis fell 8/32 to 111-20/32, Sept bills rose 0.005 to 94.230, Sept Euros were flat at 93.685. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
